'''Seaside Park''', located in [[Bridgeport, Connecticut]], is a {{convert|2.5|mi|adj=on}} long crescent-shaped park bordering [[Bridgeport Harbor]], [[Long Island Sound]], and [[Black Rock Harbor]]. The park lies within Bridgeport's South End neighborhood.<ref name="nrhpSeaside"/>

==History==
[[File:Seaside Park (Bridgeport).jpg|left|thumb|Seaside Park, before 1886]]
[[File:P. T. Barnum Monument (1887), Seaside Park, Bridgeport, CT - April 2016.JPG|left|thumb|[[P. T. Barnum]] Monument, sculpted by [[Thomas Ball (artist)|Thomas Ball]] in 1887, and placed at Seaside Park in 1893.<ref>{{cite news|title=BARNUM STATUE UNVEILED.; Bridgeport's People Pay a Tribute to the Memory of the Great Showman|url=https://query.nytimes.com/gst/abstract.html?res=9D02EFDB143EEF33A25756C0A9619C94629ED7CF|access-date=23 April 2016|work=The New York Times|date=July 5, 1893}}</ref>]]
As Bridgeport rapidly grew in population in the 19th century, residents recognized the need for more [[public parks]]. In 1863, ''The Standard'' urged the creation of one or more public parks in the city and a movement began to create a park along [[Long Island Sound]] and [[Black Rock Harbor]]. By 1864, [[P. T. Barnum]] and other residents had donated approximately {{convert|35|acre|ha}} to create Seaside Park, gradually increased to about {{convert|100|acre|ha}} by 1884.<ref>{{Cite book|ref={{SfnRef|Orcutt, v2|1886}} |author=Samuel Orcutt |title=A History of the Old Town of Stratford and City of Bridgeport Connecticut, Volume 2 |year=1886 |publisher=Fairfield County Historical Society |pages=796–798 | url=https://archive.org/stream/ahistoryoldtown01conngoog#page/n155/mode/2up }}</ref> In 1867, plans for a seawall and a driving track and walkway were made and drawings for the park were obtained from [[Frederick Law Olmsted]] whose firm completed the work. Barnum donated additional land between Iranistan Avenue, Barnum Dyke, and Waldemere Avenue in 1878. In 1866, work on a Soldiers' monument was begun and the completed monument was dedicated in 1876. In 1884, a statue of [[Elias Howe]] was added and a bronze statue of Barnum (created by [[Thomas Ball (artist)|Thomas Ball]]) was added in 1893.<ref name=waldo>{{Cite book|author=George Curtis Waldo |title=History of Bridgeport and vicinity, Volume 1 |year=1917 |publisher=S. J. Clarke |pages=277–280 |  url=https://archive.org/stream/historyofbridgep01wald#page/n337/mode/2up |isbn=978-1-144-35927-8 }}</ref> A final major monument, the William Hunt Perry Memorial Arch (designed by Henry Bacon, architect of the Lincoln Memorial in Washington, D.C.) was added in 1918. 
In 1884, Olmsted described Seaside Park as "a capital place for a drive or walk.... a fine dressy promenade."<ref name=olmsted>{{Cite book|author=F.L. & J.C. Olmsted |title=Beardsley Park: Landscape Architects' Preliminary Report |year=1884 |publisher=Privately Printed (Boston) |pages=[https://archive.org/details/beardsleyparkla00olmsgoog/page/n13 4]–5 | url=https://archive.org/details/beardsleyparkla00olmsgoog }}</ref>

In the early 1900s the park's driving track was still being used for [[horse driving]], but enthusiasts of early [[automobiles]] also raced their "[[History of steam road vehicles|steam carriages]]" and "[[History of the automobile|gasoline cars]]" on the park's track.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Driving Club's Interesting Card: Bridgeport Horsemen Enjoy Sport at seaside Park |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=b-8yAAAAIBAJ&pg=3446,2349434 |pages=1 |work=Bridgeport Herald |date=1902-05-11 |access-date=2010-08-01 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|title=Auto Racing for Bridgeport:Miles Made on Seaside Park's Flat Track in 1:35 |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=UNUyAAAAIBAJ&pg=3470,3773011 |pages=2 |work=Bridgeport Herald |date=1903-09-06 |access-date=2010-08-01 }}</ref>

The addition of [[Fayerweather Island]] in 1911 and Barnum Field in 1936, coupled with landfill operations, increased the size of the park to its present total of {{convert|375|acre|ha}}.<ref name=time2002>{{Cite news|author=Jeff Holtz |title=The View From/Bridgeport; Historic Seaside Park Recaptures Its Appeal |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2002/08/18/nyregion/the-view-from-bridgeport-historic-seaside-park-recaptures-its-appeal.html?scp=2&sq=historic%20seaside%20park%20recaptures%20its%20appeal&st=cse |work=New York Times |date=2002-08-18 |access-date=2010-08-01 }}</ref>

Seaside Park was listed on the [[National Register of Historic Places]] in 1982. [[Frederick Law Olmsted]], [[Calvert Vaux]], and Egbert Viele were the principal architects of the design. Bridgeport architect [[Ernest G. Southey]] drew plans for the Casino ('old' bath house). The site contains three major historic buildings, the Casino (1918), stables erected at the same time and, on Fayerweather Island, [[Black Rock Harbor Light]] erected in 1823.<ref name=nris/><ref name="nrhpSeaside">{{Cite web|url={{NRHP url|id=82004373}} |title=National Register of Historic Places Inventory-Nomination: Seaside Park |date = November 1981|author=Alison Gilchrist |publisher=National Park Service}} and {{NRHP url|id=82004373|title=''Accompanying 17 photographs''|photos=y}}</ref>

From 1994 to 2002, Bridgeport's Parks Department spent some $9 million on improvements. Results include a realignment of roads, more parking and a new bathhouse on the west beach with bathrooms, showers and cabanas. Not everyone was pleased about the physical changes. Charles W. Brilvitch, the city's official Historian said of the changes: "They've just disrespected the original design of the park. It was designed to have a boulevard along the waterfront, and now we've got parking lots, and we've got all this junk, this modern sculpture -- stuff that just doesn't belong in an Olmsted, Vaux and Viele park." Joe P. Gresko, the city's spokesperson, said "When Olmsted designed the park, it was back in the 1800s, when vehicles were really rare to be seen. If we kept it as is, you're asking everyone to walk to the park. I think we've improved the park. Keeping the old bathhouse and renovating it is an example of how we're trying to keep the original design in mind."<ref name=time2002/>

==Music in the park==
Seaside Park has a long history of being a venue for concerts. When the idea of Sunday concerts "for the benefit of the working people" was proposed in 1890, many neighboring residents opposed the plan, but Barnum, whose own home abutted the park, championed the cause in the local papers. When there was talk of police interference at the first concert, Barnum told the band leader to come play at his home and that the grounds would be open to all who wanted to hear the music.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Bridgeport's Great Benefactor; Mr. Barnums Home Life and His Many Philanthropic Works |url=https://query.nytimes.com/gst/abstract.html?res=980CE1DE163AE533A2575BC0A9629C94609ED7CF |quote=There was talk of police interference, and Mr. Barnum told the leader of the band to come up to Marina and play all day, and the grounds would be free to all who wished to hear the music. |pages=2 |work=New York Times |date=1891-04-08 |access-date=2010-07-29 }}</ref>

In the 1930s, the Bridgeport [[Works Progress Administration|WPA]] Orchestra, a statewide unit of the [[Federal Music Project]], gave Thursday night concerts free to the public with amplification provided by the city.<ref>{{Cite news|title=All-Russian Concert Tonight at Seaside Park in Bridgeport |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=L5k0AAAAIBAJ&pg=3219,5500973 |pages=10 |work=Norwalk Hour |date=1937-09-22 |access-date=2010-08-01 }}</ref>

Starting in summer 1999 and 2000, and every year since 2007, Seaside Park has been home to ''[[Gathering of the Vibes]]'' an annual four-day [[music]], [[camping]] and [[arts festival]] that celebrates the [[Grateful Dead]] and showcases a diverse variety of music.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.gatheringofthevibes.com/about |title=History of the Vibes |access-date=2010-07-29 |publisher=Gathering of the Vibes }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|author=Mark Zaretsky |title=Day 1 of Gathering of the Vibes in Bridgeport |url=http://www.nhregister.com/articles/2010/07/28/life/doc4c50aebad1947487201751.txt |work=New Haven Register |date=28 July 2010 |access-date=2010-07-30 }}</ref>

==Facilities==
Seaside Park offers many amenities including ball fields, picnic areas, a bathing beach, bath houses, and hiking trails. Parts of the park offering views of the water are wheelchair accessible. Food concessions, an access pier and boat launching facilities are available.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.lisrc.uconn.edu/coastalaccess/site.asp?siteid=157 |title=Connecticut Coastal Access Guide: Seaside Park |access-date=2010-07-31 |publisher=State of Connecticut }}</ref>
